chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub ibn Salim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) used to eat the vinegar and the oil, and he kept the expenditure (for it) under his carpet.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali eat and how did he store his food expenses?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the asceticism (zuhd) of Imam Ali (peace be upon him), whose staple diet of vinegar and oil symbolizes a life free from luxury and attachment to worldly comforts. By keeping the cost of these basic provisions under his carpet, he demonstrated not only personal frugality but also the practical application of simplicity in governance, serving as a model for Shia scholars on balancing spiritual humility with public leadership.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub Bin Salim who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> used eat the vinegar and the oil, and he<sup>asws</sup> kept the expenditure (for it) under his<sup>asws</sup> carpet’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya’qub ibn Salim who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
’Amir al-Mu’minin, would eat vinegar with oil and keep his expenses under the carpet.’”
